test_title: PYST 20: Selection Post (Matric Level) - English Language (Held On 26 Jun, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: english
question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1
solution:
The correct answer is '**major**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The passage discusses the significant contribution of the food industry to the GDP of India.
 
• The correct adjective should indicate that the food industry is an important area of growth.
 
• "**Major**" fits well as it denotes something important or significant, which aligns with the context of the industry's expected growth.
 
• Other options ("**superior**", "**inferior**", "**minor**") do not match the context of describing the expected growth of the industry.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

Complete Passage: *The food industry in India accounts for about 26 percent of the gross domestic product (GDP) and will be one of the major__ growth areas in the years ahead. This has given ________2______ to international trade but has also increased the responsibility to achieve the appropriate level of _____3______ in terms of sanitary and phytosanitary protection. Further, the Indian Food Safety and Standards Act of 2006, reflects a major shift in food laws and seeks to provide greater consumer protection by _________4_______ the safety and wholesomeness of food at all stages of the food chain. This changing scenario has widened the scope and ________5______ career options in this area.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 

 
• **Superior**: "Superior" means higher in rank or quality; it does not fit the context of describing growth areas.
 
• **Inferior**: "Inferior" means lower in rank or quality; it is the opposite of what is needed to describe growth.
 
• **Minor**: "Minor" means lesser in significance; it does not align with the passage's emphasis on important growth.
